purpose: A plain-language public map of current research, related experiments and supporting tools.
direction: Focus on a small number of questions that can produce evidence or useful capability. Keep supporting tools and speculative ideas secondary.

projects.title: Attention Allocation Under Cognitive Abundance
projects.summary: Study how limited human evaluation should be used when AI can produce more candidates than people can review.
projects.current_result: Track A v0.2 ended outcome-blind because admissible historical sources could not meet its frozen precision floor. In a separate review-value benchmark, disagreement was only a weak general signal, while a fixed near-boundary rule preserved 95% of pooled recommendation-side changes across fresh hold-outs with a median 45% reduction in simulated third-review work.
projects.next: Do not build a learned allocator. Design a closer-to-operational validation of the fixed near-boundary rule using sequential review state and per-stratum preservation floors.

projects.title: Personal Capability Practice
projects.summary: Test whether AI assistance can improve learning and performance in real work without leaving the human unable to understand or defend the result.
projects.current_result: The current Cognitive Kernel experiment is ready to move from prompt testing to matched real-world tasks. The useful evidence now is whether it improves outcomes while reducing rework and unnecessary human attention.
projects.next: Run the frozen pilot on real task pairs and compare completion, rework, human attention and understanding before adding more machinery.

projects.title: Nemosyne / Moneta
projects.relationship: Independent related project and experimental testbed
projects.summary: Nemosyne is an independent project that can provide concrete experiments on representation, verification and discovery without becoming part of Agalmic Research.
projects.current_result: Its useful role is specific: test measurable questions about how representations and workflows affect people. It cannot establish the wider economic or institutional claims of Agalmic Research.
projects.next: Use Nemosyne only where the intervention and outcome can be observed and measured, while keeping project ownership separate.

projects.title: Expert-Attention Preservation
projects.summary: An earlier benchmark tested what gets lost when scarce review effort is allocated by simple ranking. Its main question now feeds the broader Attention Allocation study.
projects.current_result: At a 20% review budget, ranking by post-review score preserved about 60.8% of accepted papers but only 10.0% of high-disagreement cases, compared with roughly 20% under random allocation.
projects.next: Keep the result and reuse its diagnostics where useful rather than maintaining a separate research programme.

projects.title: Research Progress Instrumentation
projects.summary: A lightweight event log for recording how candidate ideas move through selection, testing and use.
projects.current_result: The instrument exists, but it should receive more development only when it helps an active project answer a real question.
projects.next: Use it only where it reduces uncertainty or manual work in active research.
